newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke calls for lower public sector pay.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke calls for lower public sector pay.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said public sector pay awards in 1997 should be lower than in 1996. "The government remains determined to contain public spending and suggests that pay recommendations for 1997 should be set at lower levels than this year to reflect the changed economic context," he said in a statement.
In his annual submission to the Pay Review Bodies, Clarke said public sector pay settlements next year should take account of lower inflation.
"With inflation low, and expected to continue to fall, public sector settlements must adjust to reflect this, and to be affordable within budgets," he said.

Clarke said the government's approach to public sector pay had helped to deliver improved efficiency throughout the public sector, maintained firm control of public spending and provided for pay settlements at realistic and affordable levels.
Clarke also said there were no pay pressures in the economy generally.
The British government does not set pay limits centrally.
The Treasury statement said pay and price increases should be offset, or more than offset, by efficiencies and other economies.

"The approach is flexible to allow pay to be set to reflect the circumstances of individual groups, particularly by reference to the need to recruit, retain and motivate staff in the public sector within available resources," it said.

"A realistic approach to public sector pay means that headline settlements and earnings growth should be moderate and affordable and should reflect the continuing low levels of inflation," the statement added.
